order: South Korea, under interim head coach Roberto Moreno, will play two October friendlies against Venezuela and Uzbekistan, with captain Son Heung-min of LAFC chasing the all-time men's international scoring record.

The national team went 1-1 in Moreno's first two matches in September. Korea cruised past Ecuador 3-0 on consecutive goals from Oh Hyeon-gyu of Besiktas, Son and Lee Dong-gyeong of Ulsan HD, but then suffered a heavy 1-4 defeat to Uruguay. Both matches were played in a 4-4-2 formation, and attention will be on what changes Moreno makes across these two fixtures.

The first opponent, Venezuela, ranked 48th by FIFA, will be facing Korea for the first time since 2014 — a gap of 12 years. In that lone previous meeting, Korea won 3-1. Against Uzbekistan, ranked 60th, Korea hold an all-time record of 11 wins, four draws and one loss. The two matches also offer a chance to assess a regional rival ahead of next year's Asian Cup.

Son's tally rose to 58 international goals after a touch from Lee Kang-in's (Atletico Madrid) cross in the Uruguay match was credited as a goal. That figure draws him level with former head coach Cha Bum-kun at the top of the all-time men's scoring chart, and a single goal in either upcoming match would give Son the record outright.

Coupang Play analyst Lee Geun-ho said the September double-header produced contrasting results despite the same 4-4-2 setup. "It will be worth watching whether the coaching staff opts to change the tactics, the personnel, or both," he said.
Korea will face Venezuela on Friday at 8 p.m. at Munsu Football Stadium in Ulsan, then take on Uzbekistan at the same time Tuesday at Yongin Mir Stadium in Yongin, Gyeonggi Province.

Coupang Play will broadcast both matches live. Announcer Yang Dong-seok and analyst Lee Geun-ho will call the Venezuela match, while announcer Yun Jang-hyeon and analyst Im Hyeong-cheol will handle the Uzbekistan fixture.
Matches set for Friday in Ulsan, Tuesday in Yongin; tactical changes under Moreno draw attention
